findings.claim: Skilled rehabilitation need is indicated after a hospital stay, but daily need and practical-matter factors are not settled.
findings.quote: The patient requires skilled nursing services or skilled rehabilitation services
findings.case_fact: At the beginning of PT, D.E. required moderate assistance for all functional transfers.

findings.claim: Frequency of therapy (daily basis) is UNKNOWN from the case facts.
findings.quote: The patient requires these skilled services on a daily basis
findings.case_fact: the services were initiated on August 28, 2009, with treatment diagnoses of muscle weakness and lack of coordination.

findings.claim: Fluctuating vital signs led to repeated treatment changes, supporting skilled observation.
findings.quote: reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient
findings.case_fact: On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate.

findings.claim: Nurse monitoring of blood sugar logs resulted in repeated insulin changes.
findings.quote: reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary’s insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period.

findings.claim: Post-hospital hematuria with abnormal labs and bloody drainage required skilled observation.
findings.quote: Observation and assessment are skilled services when the likelihood of change in a patient’s condition requires skilled nursing
findings.case_fact: a physician indicated that the beneficiary required skilled nursing for one week to monitor for signs of fever

findings.claim: Case facts do not show the exercises or safety education needed a therapist rather than aides or nurses.
findings.quote: services can be safely and effectively performed by supportive personnel, such as aides or nursing personnel
findings.case_fact: The appellant asserts that the beneficiary made steady progress throughout physical therapy while receiving progressive resistance strengthening exercises

findings.claim: Fragility and joint hypermobility are special medical complications supporting skilled PT.
findings.quote: the particular patient’s special medical complications require the skills
findings.case_fact: the attending physician noted the beneficiary was very fragile, at Ex. 10, at 513

findings.claim: Fistula care is within the skilled wound care definition.
findings.quote: Care of wounds, (including, but not limited to, ulcers, burns, pressure sores, open surgical sites, fistulas, tube sites
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site.

findings.claim: Ostomy care reinforcement is a skilled teaching activity.
findings.quote: Teaching care for a recent ostomy or where reinforcement of ostomy care is needed
findings.case_fact: His bowel and bladder functions are maintained by colostomy and urostomy.

findings.claim: Policy sets weekly hour limits, but the hours actually furnished and their necessity are not in the case facts.
findings.quote: less than 8 hours each day and 28 or fewer hours each week
findings.case_fact: coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis

findings.claim: Case facts are procedural and contain no clinical facts to test the IRF criteria.
findings.quote: IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary under 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Social Security Act
findings.case_fact: This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004.

findings.claim: Severe pain and IV/IM medication raise doubt about ability to participate, but intensity and participation are not settled.
